evals.prompt: Here is a user story: "As a user, I want search to be fast, so that I don't get frustrated." Write proper acceptance criteria for this story, including at least one edge case, and explain what's still missing before this story could be considered ready to build.
evals.expected_output: Rewrites the vague story into concrete Given/When/Then acceptance criteria with a specific, testable threshold (e.g. a time limit) instead of the word 'fast', includes at least one edge case such as an empty or no-results query, and flags that the story as written is not testable/estimable until a concrete performance target is defined.

assertions.text: Uses Given/When/Then structure for acceptance criteria
Replaces the vague word 'fast' with a concrete, measurable criterion
Includes a specific non-happy-path scenario (empty/no-results query), not just the word 'edge case'
Flags that 'fast' as originally written is not testable

evals.prompt: Our team's proposed Definition of Done is: "Code is merged to main." Review this Definition of Done and tell me what's missing before we adopt it, and explain how a Definition of Done is different from acceptance criteria for a specific story.
evals.expected_output: Flags that this DoD is far too thin (no tests, no code review, no deployment/staging verification, no documentation update) and are not independently verifiable, and explains that DoD applies to every backlog item as a team-wide quality bar while acceptance criteria are specific to one story's expected behavior.

assertions.text: Flags that the proposed DoD is missing testing
Flags that the proposed DoD is missing code review as a distinct gap (not just echoing the word 'review' from the prompt)
Explains DoD applies to every item as a team-wide bar, not just this one story
Explains acceptance criteria are specific to a single story, tying the term to the story-specific scope rather than just naming it

evals.prompt: Review this user story against the INVEST criteria: "As a developer, I want to refactor the entire payment module to use the new internal caching layer, which depends on the caching team finishing their work first, and which will take about 6 weeks." What INVEST properties does it violate, and how would you fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the story violates Independent (blocked on another team's caching work), Small (6 weeks is far too large for a sprint), and likely Valuable (a technical refactor with no stated user-facing benefit), and recommends splitting it into smaller, independently deliverable, user-value-justified stories.

assertions.text: Identifies the Independent violation as a named INVEST property, not just quoting the prompt's dependency clause
Identifies the Small violation (6 weeks is too large for a sprint)
Recommends splitting the story into smaller pieces
